newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Peters says RBNZ won't go soft on inflation.
newsitem.headline: Peters says RBNZ won't go soft on inflation.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer Winston Peters said on Wednesday he did not expect Reserve Bank of New Zealand Governor Don Brash to go soft on inflation.

Peters, addressing parliament's finance and expenditure committee, was asked by Labour finance spokesman Michael Cullen if he expected Brash to operate monetary policy in a different way after the recent widening of the central bank's target range for underlying inflation.
"We do not expect him to go soft on inflation," Peters said.
He said Brash would be able to operate monetary policy in a smoother, more even fashion with a higher mid-point of 1.5 percent in the new 0-3 percent range.
He said this gave the governor an opportunity to better perform his role.
The target band was widened from 0-2 percent when Peters' New Zealand First Party formed a coalition last December with the conservative National Party.
